items.title: AI image generation and copyright
items.claim: The US Copyright Office issued guidance in 2023 about generative-AI images. What did it say about purely AI-generated outputs?

options.text: They are fully copyrightable by the prompter
Purely machine-generated content without human authorship is not copyrightable in the US
All such images are public domain worldwide

items.reveal_title: Human authorship is required for US copyright
items.reveal:
The US Copyright Office's March 2023 statement and subsequent rulings (e.g. Zarya of the Dawn) required identifiable human authorial contribution.

The Andersen v. Stability AI and related cases continue to test the boundaries.
items.why: Legal frameworks for what counts as an authored work are being negotiated in real time.

items.title: The painting most cited as Cubism's origin
items.claim: Which 1907 Picasso painting is most often cited as a key precursor to Cubism?
items.reveal:
Picasso painted the work in 1907 but did not exhibit it publicly until 1916. The fractured planes and reference to Iberian and African sculpture set the conditions for Cubism with Braque.

It is now in MoMA, New York.
items.why: A painting can remain influential through private circulation among artists before reaching the public.

items.title: Kahlo's body of work
items.claim: Roughly what proportion of Frida Kahlo's known paintings are self-portraits?
items.reveal_title: Roughly one third of around 150 works
items.reveal:
Standard catalogues list around 150 paintings, of which approximately 55 are self-portraits. Kahlo wrote that she painted herself 'because I am so often alone, because I am the subject I know best'.

Her first US museum retrospective opened only in 1978, 24 years after her death.
items.why: Recognition timing shapes how an artist's body of work is constructed by curators and historians.
